description: P3 consumer-assertion: docs/adr/0010-permission-allowlist-posture.md is the single home for the local-review grant posture. Local review needs no hand-written allow rule: the adaptation-cycle skill grants its one review script in allowed-tools, so no user-facing doc carries a Bash(node ...) grant. set_check in equal mode with an EMPTY expected_set over README.md (public consumers), CLAUDE.md (this repo's contributors) and web/functionality.html (site visitors) turns RED when any Bash(node ...) grant literal is added to any of the three, so an added grant is part of the threat model and needs a conscious expected_set update. The source pin spans BOTH halves of the standing rule: the discriminating scope (no local-review provider grant, codex today or ANY future provider) and the obligation it triggers (may be seeded into the committed .claude/settings.json). Narrowing the scope to codex alone, or flipping the target to the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json, unpins it. The consumer pins sit on the recorded NON-FINDING in the Findings section: its designation line, and the open question together with the 'no surface may assert it until verified empirically' prohibition. So deleting the recorded open question and silently reopening the authority vacuum fails loudly. This fixture does NOT catch: (a) a grant written in any form the extract_regex does not match, such as a Bash(bash ...) or Bash(<tool> ...) rule for a review tool, or a node grant split across lines; (b) prose in the three files that tells a reader to add a grant without writing the literal; (c) a grant added to any file not in files, which is a LITERAL list with NO glob expansion, so newly added files are invisible to it; (d) whether what any surface says is TRUE, including any claim that the skill grant suppresses the permission prompt in a subagent: a pin asserts word-sequence presence, never meaning. .claude/settings.json is deliberately NOT in files: it carries many project-specific Bash(...) grants, so equal mode there would be permanently red. Residual: the NON-FINDING designation pin embeds the recorded date, so re-dating the record trips it; the date is part of what is recorded, so that is intended.

source.pattern: No local-review provider grant — `codex` today, or any future provider (a `copilot` adapter or otherwise) — may be seeded into the committed `.claude/settings.json`.

consumers.pattern: Whether a skill's `allowed-tools` entry — for example `Bash(node *)` — suppresses the permission prompt for a provider binary invoked via node, including in a subagent context, is NOT established by this ADR's evidence. No surface in this repository may assert it until it is verified empirically against an installed Claude Code binary and the official permissions documentation.
